project.name: Ship-flow hands the Captain one UAT message instead of a chat to read
project.user_value: Kent runs one ship batch that dispatches dev entities to Conductor cloud through spacedock, from any adopter repository, without a hand-written message or a hardcoded model.
project.hypothesis: If we make the dispatch station build its message from a dev entity's stage and fix the five portability defects the adopter found, then a repository with its own ship state root dispatches two lanes to Conductor cloud through the stations, and the next batch here needs no FO rewrite of a PR body or an inline without-it pair.
project.wedge: kc-claude-plugins only; Kent as Captain; #399 (DEV-152, adopter-authored) enters at accepted; DEV-156 first because it changes what the other stations receive; then DEV-151, DEV-153, DEV-154, DEV-155. Not in it: DEV-150, nesting a first-officer session in the cloud workspace (#191's recorded ideal), the docs/plan-flow move (DEV-121, the kc-plan-flow session).
project.outcome: fenced-dispatch.sh obtains its message from spacedock dispatch build and passes the stage's model; open-pr.sh writes the pr-merge body; intent.sh/holder.sh derive branch and remote from the state checkout; e2e-gate.py takes root and flows dir as arguments; the FO skill resolves scripts from the plugin root; the accept station records an absent-at-base path the candidate adds; contract-test covers each.
exit: DEV-156, DEV-151, DEV-152 (#399), DEV-153, DEV-154, DEV-155 merged on main with contract-test green.
This batch's own PRs opened by open-pr.sh with template bodies, and its accept blocks need no inline pair duplication for new test files.
kc-ship-flow released (DEV-128 handled) so adopters install the fixed stations.

milestones.name: Ship-flow batch 2: dispatch dev entities, and the adopter portability defects

journey.persona: Kent as Captain; the relay session as adopter

journey.end: two lanes dispatched from one batch through spacedock

DEV-156.title: DEV-156
DEV-156.body:
## The problem

`kc-ship-flow/scripts/fenced-dispatch.sh` builds one hand-written message and calls `conductor workspace create --agent claude --model haiku-4-5 --effort low` (verified at main 781f9624 on 2026-09-09: line 22). The model is fixed for every batch member, and the message quality is whatever the first officer wrote that day. `spacedock dispatch build --entity-path <task> --stage <stage>` already produces an ensign dispatch artifact from a dev entity, with the model read from the workflow's stage definition (`dispatch build --print-schema` has no model field; the engine reads it per stage). Ship reinvented in bash what dev flow already owns.

Captain's ruling (recorded on spacedock-dev/subspace-relay#191, confirmed in chat 2026-09-09 「前者，先做完這一批」): the dispatch station dispatches dev entities, several in a row — one `spacedock dispatch build` call per task, one claim per task, the intent fence unchanged. The Evidence block is written after the dev task's `validation` stage (`fresh: true`, `feedback-to: implementation`) by the layer that verified, not the layer that built; `accept-evidence.sh` re-running WITHOUT_IT_COMMAND at BASE_SHA stays as a third check.

## Accepted outcome

`fenced-dispatch.sh` takes `<state-dir> <holder-id> <writer> <claim> <project-id> <base-branch> --entity-path <dev-task> --stage <stage> [--workflow-dir <dir>]`, obtains the message by running `spacedock dispatch build --entity-path … --stage … --host claude` (the artifact's text is the message file whose sha256 the intent records), passes no `--model`/`--effort` to `conductor workspace create` unless the built artifact carries one, and refuses with a named reason when `dispatch build` exits non-zero. The station doc states that the dispatched unit is a dev entity and that the Evidence block arrives from the task's validation stage. Falsifier: a fixture dev task whose stage declares a model produces a create call carrying that model; the same task with no model produces a create call with none.

## Non-goals

* Nesting a first-officer session in the cloud workspace (recorded on #191 as the ideal, not this ticket).
* Changing the intent/holder fence or the claim schema.
* Changing [accept-evidence.sh](<http://accept-evidence.sh>)'s checks.

## Acceptance criteria

* **AC-1** `bash kc-ship-flow/scripts/fenced-dispatch.sh <fixture-state> h1 1 dev-1.g1 <uuid> main --entity-path kc-ship-flow/scripts/fixtures/dispatch/task-with-model.md --stage implementation --dry-run` prints the `conductor workspace create` argv containing `--model` from the stage and the message sha256 that matches the built artifact.
* **AC-2** the same with `--entity-path …/task-without-model.md` prints an argv without `--model` and `--effort`.
* **AC-3** `python3 kc-ship-flow/scripts/contract-test.py` exits 0 with both fixtures registered, and a fixture whose `dispatch build` fails makes the script exit 4 printing `dispatch build failed`.

Re-verified: `grep -c 'model haiku-4-5' /Users/kent/.claude/plugins/local/kc-ship-flow/scripts/fenced-dispatch.sh` exit 0 2026-09-09

DEV-155.title: DEV-155
DEV-155.body:
## The problem

Observed 2026-09-09 on iamcxa/kc-claude-plugins#399 (DEV-152) by the subspace-relay session, and consistent with [accept-evidence.sh](<http://accept-evidence.sh>)'s AC-1 at main: the station runs WITHOUT_IT_COMMAND in a worktree at BASE_SHA and requires a non-zero exit there; when the pair lives in a test file the candidate adds, `bash` on the missing file exits 127, which the station refuses as "command did not run" (the S43-era rule that a command must have run, not merely failed). The worker's only way through is to duplicate the new test's assertion inline in WITHOUT_IT_COMMAND — so the pair and the test can drift and nothing checks that they still agree. The same shape hit DEV-148 and DEV-149 (fixture directories absent at BASE_SHA).

## Accepted outcome

The station distinguishes "the command's own file is absent at BASE_SHA" from "the command ran and failed": when WITHOUT_IT_COMMAND names a path that is added by the candidate (present at CANDIDATE_SHA, absent at BASE_SHA — the station already computes the changed-path set), the BASE_SHA leg is satisfied by that fact and recorded as `at BASE_SHA: absent (added by candidate)` instead of demanding an exit code; the removed-variant leg still must run at CANDIDATE_SHA and fail. An absent path that the candidate did not add is still refused. Contract cases: a pair whose command is a new test file → ACCEPT with the recorded reason; a pair naming a path absent on both sides → REFUSE.

## Non-goals

* Relaxing the removed-variant leg.
* Accepting a pair with no observable failure at all.

## Acceptance criteria

* **AC-1** `bash kc-ship-flow/scripts/accept-evidence.sh kc-ship-flow/scripts/fixtures/new-test-file-pair.md` prints ACCEPT and `at BASE_SHA: absent (added by candidate)`.
* **AC-2** `bash kc-ship-flow/scripts/accept-evidence.sh kc-ship-flow/scripts/fixtures/mutant-absent-both-sides.md` prints REFUSE naming the path.
* **AC-3** `python3 kc-ship-flow/scripts/contract-test.py` exits 0 with both fixtures registered.

Re-verified: `grep -c 'at BASE_SHA' /Users/kent/.claude/plugins/local/kc-ship-flow/scripts/accept-evidence.sh` exit 0 2026-09-09

DEV-154.title: DEV-154
DEV-154.body:
## The problem

Reported by the subspace-relay adopter on 2026-09-09, verified: `kc-ship-flow/skills/first-officer/SKILL.md` names every station script as `kc-ship-flow/scripts/<name>` (lines 17, 29–35 at main). In an adopter repository the plugin is installed under the Claude/Codex plugin root, not at that relative path, so the FO cannot run the chain as written.

## Accepted outcome

The skill resolves the scripts directory once (the plugin's own install path via `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}` or the skill file's location) and names each script relative to it; docs/ship/README.md's per-stage lines are pinned to the same resolution; [local-profile-check.py](<http://local-profile-check.py>) verifies the resolved paths exist. Falsifier: the chain runs from a temp adopter checkout with the plugin installed only under ~/.claude/plugins/local/.

## Non-goals

* Moving scripts out of the plugin.
* Changing what each station does.

## Acceptance criteria

* **AC-1** `python3 kc-ship-flow/scripts/local-profile-check.py kc-ship-flow/scripts/fixtures/adopter/docs/ship/README.md` run from a directory that is not kc-claude-plugins exits 0 and prints each resolved script path.
* **AC-2** `grep -c 'kc-ship-flow/scripts/' kc-ship-flow/skills/first-officer/SKILL.md` prints 0 (paths come from the resolved root).
* **AC-3** `python3 kc-ship-flow/scripts/contract-test.py` exits 0 with the adopter fixture registered.

Re-verified: `grep -c 'kc-ship-flow/scripts/' /Users/kent/.claude/plugins/local/kc-ship-flow/skills/first-officer/SKILL.md` exit 0 2026-09-09

DEV-153.title: DEV-153
DEV-153.body:
## The problem

Reported by the subspace-relay adopter on 2026-09-09, verified on kc-claude-plugins main: `kc-ship-flow/scripts/e2e-gate.py` line 43 `ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2]` lands outside any checkout when the plugin is installed under ~/.claude/plugins/local/; it degrades to `e2e: not applicable` only because the flow-file check runs before `resolve_commit`. Line 44 `FLOWS_DIR = ROOT / "docs/ship-flow/flows"` names the retired workflow (DEV-120) while the commissioned docs/ship/README.md Local Profile row says `docs/ship/flows/`.

## Accepted outcome

[e2e-gate.py](<http://e2e-gate.py>) takes the repository root and the flows directory from its arguments (the FO skill passes the code checkout root and the README's Local Profile row), never from `__file__`; a missing flows directory is a named refusal, not "not applicable"; the station doc and SKILL.md show the invocation.

## Non-goals

* Changing the flow-file format or [e2e-cli.sh](<http://e2e-cli.sh>).
* Retiring docs/ship-flow (DEV-120).

## Acceptance criteria

* **AC-1** `python3 kc-ship-flow/scripts/e2e-gate.py --root kc-ship-flow/scripts/fixtures/e2e-gate/repo --flows docs/ship/flows <milestone>` exits 0 and prints the resolved flow path under docs/ship/flows.
* **AC-2** the same with `--flows docs/missing` exits 2 and prints `flows directory not found`.
* **AC-3** `python3 kc-ship-flow/scripts/contract-test.py` exits 0 with both fixtures registered.

Re-verified: `grep -c 'docs/ship-flow/flows' /Users/kent/.claude/plugins/local/kc-ship-flow/scripts/e2e-gate.py` exit 0 2026-09-09

DEV-152.title: DEV-152
DEV-152.body:
## The problem

Reported by the subspace-relay adopter session on 2026-09-09 and verified by the FO on kc-claude-plugins main the same day: `kc-ship-flow/scripts/intent.sh` line 11 and `kc-ship-flow/scripts/holder.sh` line 9 set `branch=spacedock-state/dev` and use it for `fetch`, `merge --ff-only FETCH_HEAD` and `push origin HEAD:$branch`; `fenced-dispatch.sh` calls both. A repository whose `docs/ship` state root sits on `spacedock-state/ship` (subspace-relay has three roots: dev, plan, ship) would push ship's intents and holder record onto dev's branch. The value is an assumption from when this repository's ship state lived under docs/dev on that branch, not a constraint.

## Accepted outcome

Both scripts derive the branch from the state checkout itself — `git -C "$state" rev-parse --abbrev-ref --symbolic-full-name @{upstream}` (falling back to `rev-parse --abbrev-ref HEAD` with `origin/` prefix) — and refuse with a named reason when the checkout has no upstream; [fenced-dispatch.sh](<http://fenced-dispatch.sh>) passes nothing new. Falsifier: a temp state checkout on branch `spacedock-state/ship` with an origin, `intent.sh commit` pushes to `spacedock-state/ship` and `git -C origin rev-parse spacedock-state/dev` is unchanged.

## Non-goals

* Parametrising the branch on the command line (a second source of truth beside the checkout).
* Changing the claim/intent schema.

## Acceptance criteria

* **AC-1** `bash kc-ship-flow/scripts/intent.sh commit <ship-root-fixture> h1 1 dev-1.g1 <token> <uuid> main <sha>` in a fixture whose state checkout tracks `origin/spacedock-state/ship` exits 0 and `git -C <origin> log -1 --format=%s spacedock-state/ship` prints the intent commit while `spacedock-state/dev` is untouched.
* **AC-2** the same with a checkout that has no upstream exits 6 and prints `state checkout has no upstream`.
* **AC-3** `python3 kc-ship-flow/scripts/contract-test.py` exits 0 with both fixtures registered.

Re-verified: `git show origin/main:kc-ship-flow/scripts/intent.sh | grep -q 'branch=spacedock-state/dev'` exit 0 2026-09-09

DEV-151.title: DEV-151
DEV-151.body:
## The problem

Captain, 2026-09-09: 「應該要按照 pr-mod 寫 pr body」. `kc-ship-flow/scripts/open-pr.sh` writes a body of five lines (Candidate, Base, Without-it, Removed variant, Accept station) — verified by reading its BODY_EOF heredoc on 2026-09-09 — while the repository's pr-merge mod (`docs/dev/_mods/pr-merge.md` § PR body template) requires: a one-sentence motivation lead (≤25 words), `## What changed` (3–5 action-verb bullets ≤15 words), `## Evidence` (N/N passed per suite), a `---` separator, the audit link `[{entity-id}](/{owner}/{repo}/blob/{sha}/{path})`, and `Closes {issue}`; 60–120 words. In batch c5a7274dd07c the workers opened PRs themselves with free-form bodies (#395, #397); the FO rewrote #397 by hand.

## Accepted outcome

`open-pr.sh <evidence-file> <batch-dir>` builds the pr-merge body from the Evidence block, the plan receipt's issue entry (motivation lead condensed from `## The problem`, `Fixes <issue>` from `close_line`) and the batch README (audit link to the batch entity on the state branch), with `## Evidence` from the block's TESTS line in N/N form; the body is 60–120 words; contract-test asserts the section order and the Closes line. Falsifier: #397's rewritten body, regenerated by the script from its evidence file, differs only in wording of the lead.

## Non-goals

* Changing the pr-merge mod's template.
* Generating the PR title (already the candidate commit's subject).

## Acceptance criteria

* **AC-1** `bash kc-ship-flow/scripts/open-pr.sh kc-ship-flow/scripts/fixtures/open-pr/evidence.md kc-ship-flow/scripts/fixtures/open-pr/batch --dry-run` prints a body whose first line has no `#` and ≤25 words and whose sections appear in the order What changed, Evidence, `---`, audit link, Fixes.
* **AC-2** the same with a block lacking TESTS prints a body without `## Evidence` and exits 0.
* **AC-3** `python3 kc-ship-flow/scripts/contract-test.py` exits 0 with both fixtures registered.

Re-verified: `grep -c 'What changed' /Users/kent/.claude/plugins/local/kc-ship-flow/scripts/open-pr.sh` exit 1 2026-09-09
